extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies, regulated sources, and members of the public submitting comments on EPA SIP/RACT actions (environmental stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_short: commenting on EPA SIP RACT proposal
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit public comments (and supporting materials) on EPA's supplemental proposed rule to approve Texas' SIP RACT (VOC) determinations for the HGB 2008 ozone serious nonattainment area. Includes procedural requirements for submissions and substantive criteria EPA uses to evaluate RACT/ SIP approvability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments close / deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Written comments must be received on or before August 25, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submission is completed and received by the deadline; late comments may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments (docket identification and channels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your comments, identified by Docket No. EPA-R06-OAR-2020-0165, at https://www.regulations.gov or via email to Shahin.emad@epa.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions for submitting comments. For additional submission methods, contact the listed EPA official. Once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed from Regulations.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) and restricted disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit electronically any information you consider to be Confidential Business Information (CBI) or other information whose disclosure is restricted by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA may redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof) from public view. If you need to provide CBI or materials not suitable for the public docket, contact the EPA official for alternative submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia submissions requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia submissions (audio, video, etc.) must be accompanied by a written comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written comment is considered the official comment and should include discussion of all points you wish to make. EPA will generally not consider comments or comment contents located outside of the primary submission (i.e., on the web, cloud, or other file sharing system).

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA public comment policy and publication of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA may publish any comment received to its public docket. Agencies review all submissions and may choose to redact, or withhold, certain submissions (or portions thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once submitted, comments cannot be edited or removed from Regulations.gov. See the full EPA public comment policy for detailed instructions and guidance on making effective comments: https://www.epa.gov/dockets/commenting-epa-dockets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket index availability and access limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The index to the docket for this action is available electronically at www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While all documents in the docket are listed in the index, some information may not be publicly available due to docket file size restrictions or content (e.g., CBI). If you need alternative access to material indexed but not provided in the docket, contact the EPA official.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory standard for SIP approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Clean Air Act, the Administrator is required to approve a SIP submission that complies with the provisions of the Clean Air Act and applicable Federal regulations (42 U.S.C. 7410(k); 40 CFR 52.02(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's role is to approve state choices, provided that they meet the criteria of the Clean Air Act; EPA cannot impose additional requirements beyond those imposed by state law when approving a SIP that complies with Federal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: RACT applicability (which sources require RACT)
rubrics_metrics.description: CAA sections 182(b)(2) and (f) require that SIPs for ozone nonattainment areas classified as Moderate or higher include implementation of RACT for any source covered by a CTG document and also for any major source of VOC or NOx.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether a source is covered by a Control Techniques Guideline (CTG) category or meets the major source threshold (e.g., Serious area major source definition = 50 tpy for VOCs in this document).

rubrics_metrics.name: RACT definition (the substantive control standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: RACT is defined by EPA as 'the lowest emissions limitation that a particular source is capable of meeting by the application of control technology that is reasonably available, considering technological and economic feasibility.' (See 44 FR 53761, Sept. 17, 1979.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RACT determinations must consider both technical feasibility and economic feasibility when determining the lowest achievable emission limitation reasonably available to a source.

rubrics_metrics.name: RACT evaluation methods and comparative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA evaluated relevant RACT rules by reviewing state rules across multiple states (Arizona, California, Colorado, Illinois, Indiana, Maine, New Hampshire, Ohio, Vermont, and Wisconsin), comparing Texas' rules to control measures in other states and CTGs, and reviewing the RACT/BACT/LAER clearinghouse for required technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-state comparisons, CTG consistency checks, and information from the RACT/BACT/LAER clearinghouse; EPA looks for whether state rules are 'generally consistent with or more stringent than' measures elsewhere and whether there are new control technologies reasonably available considering technical and economic feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of 'reasonably available' new control technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA assesses whether it has identified any new control technologies that are 'reasonably available' considering technological and economic feasibility for the affected sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If EPA identifies new reasonably available technologies, that may affect whether state rules meet RACT; absence of such technologies supports a finding that existing rules remain representative of RACT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative declarations (when EPA may approve them)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may approve state negative declarations for certain CTG categories if justified (EPA proposed to approve negative declarations for fiberglass boat manufacturing materials, pneumatic rubber tires manufacturing, flat wood paneling coatings, letterpress printing, and automobile and light‑duty truck assembly coatings sectors in the HGB area).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A negative declaration should be supported in the SIP submission showing that no sources in the area are subject to the CTG category or that RACT is otherwise not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency response to public comment and supplemental analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: If comments claim reliance on outdated determinations, EPA may provide additional analysis and supplement its proposal (as EPA supplemented the March 2021 proposal with a Supplemental TSD and invited comment on the supplemental analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public commenters can prompt EPA to provide further analysis; EPA will address comments received on both the original proposal and any supplemental proposal in its final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official Federal Register/PDF for legal notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The FederalRegister.gov XML rendition is an unofficial informational resource and does not replace the official print edition or the official electronic PDF on govinfo.gov; until the ACFR grants official status, the XML rendition does not provide legal notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For legal research and official citations, verify contents against the official PDF on govinfo.gov (FR Doc. citation provided).
